fact_text: In 2025 the farmer's area had poor rain and about six months without drinking water, and the farm's running and land costs were not covered, so he looked at fish farming on groundwater.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farm started with 36 tanks of 20 ft each and a capital investment of about 15 million; the owner set it up as a full business, not a side income. The currency is not stated in the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: After adding larger cemented tanks with a semi-recirculating (RAS-type) water system, the farm's capacity rose from about 20 tons a year to about 50 tons a year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer's stated target is 500 tons a year within five years from 2026, up from about 50 tons; this is a management aim, not a result.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: A shrimp hatchery the farmer visited in Thailand reportedly sells about 10 million seed a day, both for export and for local supply.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Pakistan has no domestic Asian sea bass seed; the fish is only available as wild catch, and wild fish cannot be bred in farm tanks, which the farmer says is the main barrier for this species.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer said Asian sea bass has export buyers at any time of year, so a farm that can supply seed or fish has a year-round outlet.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: BR Hatchery (Private) Limited, a hatchery at Hawks Bay set up by the same farmer after the Thailand visit, aims to breed Asian sea bass seed in Pakistan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: From 2027 the hatchery plans to supply 3 to 4 inch Asian sea bass seed to fish farmers across Pakistan; this is a stated plan, not an achieved result.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Waste feed and fish waste settle at the tank bottom and rot if the slope is wrong, producing ammonia that fouls the water and kills fish.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer advises the owner to personally check tank design, the slope and the pipe quality, because builders often use thin pipes to save cost.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: A common 100-watt aerator runs around the clock for a whole year, which limits its life; the farmer runs two units for 12 hours each so each can cool.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Solar alone is not enough for an aerated tank farm; reliable grid electricity and a UPS backup are needed, because aerators stop the oxygen supply when power fails.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Algae produce oxygen in the water during the day, but oxygen falls at night, so most fish die around dawn, roughly 4 to 5 am, before the water recovers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: About 50 fish in a tank need no extra aeration, but 3,000 fish need mechanical oxygen, much as a room that holds 100 people is hard to breathe in.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: According to the farmer, 50 tons a year from one acre of tank space equals the output of about 25 to 30 acres of pond farming.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Fish farming runs in three stages: a hatchery for fingerlings, a nursery, and grow-out; many farmers skip the nursery and stock bought fingerlings straight into grow-out.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Many farmers stock 700 to 800 fingerlings straight into grow-out without grading, and the farmer says this leaves the size spread uncontrolled.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Fast-growing 'shooter' fish eat first and push smaller fish off the feed, so the farmer grades stock every two to three weeks rather than once.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: A 2-gram fingerling can become a 12-gram shooter, and shooters keep the smaller fish from feeding, so their gap widens over time.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: About 10% of stocked fish are genetically stunted and do not grow, the farmer says.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Stunted fish should be removed early, because keeping them in the tank keeps raising feed cost without any growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Tilapia reach about 500 g in six months, and holding them for a full year reached about 1 kg.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer judged a 1 kg harvest not viable at the cost of holding fish for a year; the usual harvest is at 500 to 600 g.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Quoted market rate on 6 Nov 2026 was 600 PKR per kg for fish and 500 PKR for half-kilo fish; the currency is read as PKR from the rupee symbol.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Market buyers grade the fish themselves and pack them in 20 kg crates; 600 g and 700 g fish sell in the half-kilo bracket and miss the per-kg price.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: After the first market sale the farmer stopped selling in the wholesale market and switched to vendors who also export.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: A well-managed tank with a good system yields about 650 to 700 kg of fish meat per cycle, the farmer said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: A farm manager checks oxygen, pH and temperature in every tank each morning and evening and reports the readings, while four labourers handle cleaning and daily tasks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Labour works only when the owner is present, so the farmer uses a manager and cameras, and visits three to four times a week for two to four hours each visit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Each tank is cleaned within 15 days after harvest, and the farm plans to restock 55,000 fingerlings at the end of March 2027 into its new nursery.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farm runs two six-month cycles: one stocked in October 2026, harvested in June 2027 at 500 to 600 g, and a second harvested in December 2027, aiming for about 50 tons in total.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Aqua OS is a farm-management app built internally by the farmer, logging stocking per tank, calculating daily feed, tracking pH and oxygen, and recording costs; it is in final internal testing before launch.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The app's mortality tool lets a farmer check the data from the one to two days before a loss to see what caused unexpected fish deaths.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer advises that a business needs at least 10 to 12 tanks; the 4 to 10 tank set-ups promoted on social media are not viable, in his view.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: Fish farming is not a side hustle: it needs close attention around the clock, because a power cut can ruin a tank and labour cannot be left to run it alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer says a new fish farm needs at least two years before it is run as a business, because the first six months are spent learning feeding, disease and oxygen management.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)

fact_text: The farmer said Pakistan's fish farming still uses traditional methods with very low efficiency, which is why he visited Thailand to learn modern practice.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From Farming Losses To Fish Farming Success | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-06)
